hints: Look at how many bonding pairs and lone pairs surround each central atom for x, y and z, as this controls the shape.
Notice that the carbon in angle y has four bonding pairs and no lone pairs, so it will be close to the ideal tetrahedral angle.
Compare the S atom with two lone pairs to the N atom with one lone pair, and remember that lone pair repulsion squeezes bond angles more strongly.
walkthrough:
**Identify the electron pairs at each centre**

Think of each angle as telling you about the shape around its middle atom. Count bonding pairs and lone pairs carefully.

For $x$ (H-S-C): S has 2 bonds + 2 lone pairs = 4 pairs. For $y$ (H-C-C): C has 4 bonds + 0 lone pairs = 4 pairs. For $z$ (C-N-H): N has 3 bonds + 1 lone pair = 4 pairs.

**Apply VSEPR repulsion order**

Remember the golden rule: lone pair-lone pair > lone pair-bond pair > bond pair-bond pair in repulsion strength. More lone pairs means more squeezing of the bond angle.

$$\text{ideal tetrahedral} \approx 109.5^{\circ} > \text{pyramidal with 1 lone pair} \approx 107^{\circ} > \text{bent with 2 lone pairs} \approx 104.5^{\circ}$$

**Rank x, y and z from largest to smallest**

Angle y has no lone pairs, so it stays largest at about $109.5^{\circ}$. Angle z has one lone pair, so it is slightly squeezed to about $107^{\circ}$. Angle x has two lone pairs, so it is squeezed most.

$$y > z > x$$

options.A: Incorrect. This puts x as largest, but S in angle x has two lone pairs which repel very strongly and make x the smallest, not the largest.
options.B: Incorrect. This also puts x as largest. Students choosing this often forget to count both lone pairs on sulfur and treat it like a tetrahedral carbon.
options.C: Correct. y is tetrahedral with 4 bonding pairs (about 109.5 degrees), z is pyramidal with 1 lone pair (about 107 degrees), and x is bent with 2 lone pairs (about 104.5 degrees or less), so y > z > x.
options.D: Incorrect. This correctly puts x as smallest but swaps y and z. Remember one lone pair on N still squeezes the angle below the perfect tetrahedral angle at C, so y must be larger than z.
